description: Records that some data existed by a block: give the SHA-256 of a file or text (64 hexadecimal characters; compute it yourself and never send the data itself). Free of charge, within a daily bound for all callers together and a smaller one for the internet address a request comes from, which many users of one application may share. Stamps are written in batches about every ten minutes: the first answer says "waiting" and when the next batch is; call again with the same sha256 after it and one block (about 15 minutes in all) and the answer is the proof (state "stamped"). Asking again within seven days for a hash taken through this connector costs nothing. Keep the proof. Anyone can check it without trusting Polarka: polarka-agent stamp-verify with their own TrueNorth node, or the transaction and its block in an explorer of the chain. north_stamp_verify checks it here, with Polarka's node. The hash of a short or guessable text can be guessed back: add a random secret and keep it. TrueNorth is young and small: a stamp is evidence of order in time, not proof for a court.

sha256.description: the SHA-256 of the data, 64 hexadecimal characters
